title: Why Palestine Matters to Muslims
subtitle: Why Muslims love Al-Aqsa and seek justice for Palestine
summary: Palestine matters to Muslims because Al-Aqsa is a blessed sanctuary tied to the Prophet's night journey, the history of revelation, and the first direction of prayer. Islam also commands Muslims to defend justice, protect human dignity, and speak truthfully about the suffering of the oppressed.

sections.title: Why Palestine Matters to Muslims
sections.body: Muslims speak about Palestine with special concern because Jerusalem and Al-Aqsa have a central place in Islamic faith and history. That concern includes love for a sacred place, solidarity with people facing displacement or injustice, and a desire for peace rooted in truth. It does not require Muslims to ignore the dignity, grief, or religious attachments of anyone else.

sections.title: Religious Connection
sections.body: The Quran says that Allah took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings He blessed (Quran 17:1). Muslim hadith and tafsir identify the Farthest Mosque with the sanctuary in Jerusalem. Al-Aqsa is also linked in Islamic tradition with earlier prophets and with the first direction of prayer. This religious connection is why Muslims love the site and feel responsible for its protection.

sections.title: Religious Concern Must Remain Ethical
sections.body:
Islamic concern for a sacred place must remain concern for people. The Quran commands justice even when emotions are strong: "do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just" (Quran 5:8). Muslims should oppose oppression and protect civilians while rejecting anti-Jewish hatred, anti-Christian hostility, collective blame, and unverified stories. Compassion is not weakened by accuracy; it depends on it.

The Quran also describes people expelled from their homes and mentions monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques as places where God's name is remembered (Quran 22:40). A Muslim response to Palestine should therefore combine love of Al-Aqsa with worship, truthful speech, mercy, and practical concern for every innocent person.

sections.title: Key Takeaways: Why Palestine Matters to Muslims
sections.body: Palestine matters to Muslims because Al-Aqsa is a blessed sanctuary connected to the Prophet's night journey and the history of revelation. It also matters because Islam commands justice, protection of human dignity, and truthful concern for people facing oppression. A sincere Muslim response holds both commitments together: honor Al-Aqsa and stand for justice without hatred, falsehood, or harm to the innocent.

quranVerses.arabic: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ سُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِۦ لَيْلًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ إِلَى ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْأَقْصَا ٱلَّذِى بَٰرَكْنَا حَوْلَهُۥ لِنُرِيَهُۥ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَآ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْبَصِيرُ
quranVerses.translation: Exalted is He who took His Servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوا۟ قَوَّٰمِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَآءَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ ۖ وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوْمٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا۟ ۚ ٱعْدِلُوا۟ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
quranVerses.translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا۟ مِن دِيَٰرِهِم بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّآ أَن يَقُولُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ۗ وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ لَّهُدِّمَتْ صَوَٰمِعُ وَبِيَعٌۭ وَصَلَوَٰتٌۭ وَمَسَٰجِدُ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ كَثِيرًۭا ۗ وَلَيَنصُرَنَّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُۥٓ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ
quranVerses.translation: [They are] those who have been evicted from their homes without right - only because they say, "Our Lord is Allah." And were it not that Allah checks the people, some by means of others, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned. And Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation
